title: Console insights: tiered card + fallback plan to constrain surface area for alpha
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: we need a targeted rescope of the Console Insights surface for alpha so we ship by the end of April with low operational cost and clear rollback paths. This ticket captures the approved approach: present a single 'tiered card' pattern (summary -> detail pane) across dashboards, tracing, and per-route cost breakdown. The goal is to reduce distinct UI flows, limit backend telemetry retention for alpha, and provide graceful degraded modes when sampled telemetry is unavailable.

Scope decision summary:
- Keep: route-level cost estimator (summary metrics), single-card trace timeline with sample selection, and a compact latency histogram.
- Defer: full-session flamegraphs, per-token cost attribution, long-term retention (>30d) analytics, and per-request payload inspection.
- Add fallback: when tracing samples are missing or delayed, surface a deterministic percent-of-requests estimate and a link to historical sampling coverage.

Why this approach: consolidating visualization into a tiered card reduces engineering breadth (fewer backend indexes + fewer bespoke queries), limits frontend routes and state management, and gives us a simple A/B path to reintroduce more advanced views post-alpha. The fallback ensures customers don't see empty pages and retains a path to investigate production gaps.

What this ticket contains: PRD-level acceptance criteria, rollout plan for alpha (canary to 5% orgs), instrumentation checklist, and a minimal set of backend retention/aggregation knobs needed for the tiered card.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Tiered card is the only insights surface visible in alpha; it must render summary metrics within 1s for cached requests and within 3s for cold queries.
2) Trace timeline displays up to 50 sampled spans and shows sample coverage percent; missing-sample fallback displays an estimate with a clear CTA to 'Request fresh sample'.
3) Route cost summary shows last-24h and rolling-7d aggregates; per-route cost delta must be computed by an aggregation pipeline that runs within our existing hourly batch window.
4) No alpha org receives the detailed views we deferred (flamegraphs, per-token attribution). Attempts to access them return a consistent UX with an explanation and an 'Invite to beta' CTA.
5) Rollout includes a canary toggle in console feature flags and monitoring dashboards for page load SLO (p95 < 2.5s) and backend query latency (p95 < 800ms).
6) Operational playbook added linking to incident runbook and steps to revert to a static summary tile if backend errors exceed thresholds.
decision_rationale: Primary constraints were delivery window and backend indexing cost. The tiered card gives the most signal per engineering effort and minimizes new storage/indexing needs. Deferments were chosen to avoid building high-cardinality joins and to keep retention short for alpha which reduces storage egress and privacy surface. Fallback UX ensures customers see useful information even when tracing sampling is offline.
tradeoffs:
- Reduced forensic tooling in alpha may slow root cause analysis for complex incidents.
- Sampling-based tracing presents less deterministic views; we add explicit coverage indicators to mitigate trust issues.
- Short retention reduces longitudinal insights; we will add export hooks for customers who need longer windows in dedicated/private later.
